meta.title: Lesson 5 data: capacity factors, the year profiles' targets, the solar day and the illustrative turbine

meta.about: The wind and solar shapes in town_year.json are each divided by their own 2025 maximum hour, so their mean is NOT a capacity factor (wind 0.528, solar 0.238). The lesson turns them into a plant's output with the shared helper LX.townProfile (assets/learn/components/profiles.js), method "power", to the annual targets in the shared cf_targets.json (EIA Table 6.07.B, 2025), after two lesson-local steps: night-time solar telemetry set to zero (solarClean) and each month brought to the 2025 U.S. monthly capacity factor (monthly_2025). Nuclear runs at full size except for one illustrative refuelling outage (nuclear). Why "power": the best hours reach the plant's size, so the year view shows output against nameplate.

monthly_2025.about: Monthly capacity factor of U.S. utility-scale generators in 2025, January to December (EIA Table 6.07.B, final). Used in Go deeper.
monthly_2025.source: cf_targets.json source (EIA, Electric Power Monthly, Table 6.07.B, data for August 2026, released 23 October 2026; 2025 values final)

year.about: town_year.json: index i is the hour ending at start_utc + i (UTC). start_utc is 2025-01-01T07:00, so index 0 is the hour 00:00-01:00 Central Standard Time on 1 January and the 8,760 hours make 365 whole local days (standard time, UTC-6, all year).

solarClean.about: Night-time telemetry in the SPP solar shape (18 February to 21 March 2025 and a few other nights; 370 hours, 1.3% of the shape's energy) is set to zero before rescaling: an hour is night when the sun is below the horizon at the start and the end of the hour at all four corners of this box, which spans the Southwest Power Pool's solar farms (simple solar geometry, 05-capacity-factor.js sunUp).

nuclear.about: Illustrative: the plant runs at full size all year except one spring refuelling outage of 780 hours (32.5 days, from 25 March), so that the year's capacity factor is (8760 - 780) / 8760 = 91.1%, the 2025 U.S. average. EIA: plants refuel every 18 to 24 months, mostly in spring and fall; the average planned outage in 2022 lasted 38 days.

day.about: The solar day: the 100 MW solar farm's hourly output on the lesson-0 day, Central daylight time (UTC-5), rounded to whole MW.

turbine.about: Illustrative onshore turbine with a clean power curve: below the rated speed the output follows the cube law, P = rated x (v / ratedSpeed)^3; from the rated speed to the cut-out speed it holds its rated power; outside [cutIn, cutOut] it makes nothing. With a 100 m rotor and air at 1.225 kg/m3 this is a power coefficient of 0.36 at the rated speed, below the Betz limit 16/27.

apply.about: Step 8: Prairie Town's wind farm (town.json fleet.wind.mw) at the 2025 U.S. wind capacity factor.
